title: Milky Way emerges as Sun sets over Paranal
caption: The Milky Way behind Unit Telescope 4, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: As the Sun sets over ESO's Paranal Observatory, the Milky Way emerges in fine detail behind Unit Telescope 4, known as Yepun. Paranal is home to the Very Large Telescope, the flagship facility of European ground-based astronomy.
To the naked eye, the Milky Way looks like a cloudy haze across the sky. In reality it is made of 100–400 billion individual stars spread along its 100 000 light-year length.

Yepun is the word for Venus in the language of the Mapuche, the indigenous people of southern Chile. It belongs to a set of four 8.2-meter telescopes that can be combined to act as one giant telescope, letting astronomers see details up to 16 times finer than any single telescope could. Working together, the VLT has opened a new age of discovery, with several notable scientific firsts, among them following single stars as they orbit the supermassive black hole at our galaxy's center.
